messages.author: fb40a65bd21dcf6f
messages.subject: Noisy Poisson counts
parts:
Hi,

First of all thanks for Stan, it really seems well engineered and extremely useful for continuous data. That said I'm having a few problems with count data. I want to model counts as some sum over a true count and a noisy count (distributed as a Poisson with a relatively small rate). I've tried to set the model up as below but I'm running into a problem whereby Stan won't let me have integer parameters. Is Stan just not suitable for this sort of model? Perhaps there is some reparameterisation I haven't thought of that could help? The code belows samples data from the model in R and then tries to build a Stan model to fit it. I have a matrix of counts where each column has a scaling factor for both the rates of the noise and of the true counts. Each row has its own rate for the true counts. The observed counts are the sum of the noise and the true counts. I know it could be vectorized more efficiently but I need to get it working first.

N <-  10  # Number of rows                                                                                                                                                                                        
M <-   3  # Number of columns                                                                                                                                                                                     
col.sizes <- rlnorm(M, 0, 1)  # Scaling factor for each column                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
# Generate noise for each column                                                                                                                                                                                  
noise.lambda <- 1                                                                                                                                                                                                 
noise <- matrix(0, nrow=N, ncol=M)                                                                                                                                                                                
for(m in 1:M) {                                                                                                                                                                                                   
    noise[,m] <- rpois(N, noise.lambda * col.sizes[m])                                                                                                                                                            
}                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
# Generate true counts                                                                                                                                                                                            
counts.lambda <- rlnorm(N, 2, 3)                                                                                                                                                                                  
counts <- matrix(0, nrow=N, ncol=M)                                                                                                                                                                               
for(n in 1:N) {                                                                                                                                                                                                   
    for(m in 1:M) {                                                                                                                                                                                               
        counts[n,m] <- rpois(1, counts.lambda[n] * col.sizes[m])                                                                                                                                                  
    }                                                                                                                                                                                                             
}                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
# Observed counts are true counts + noise                                                                                                                                                                         
obs.counts <- counts + noise                                                                                                                                                                                      
obs.counts                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
# Code as a Stan model                                                                                                                                                                                            
stan.code <- '                                                                                                                                                                                                    
data {                                                                                                                                                                                                            
    int<lower=0> N;  # Number of rows                                                                                                                                                                             
    int<lower=0> M;  # Number of columns                                                                                                                                                                          
    int<lower=0> obs[N,M];  # Observed counts                                                                                                                                                                     
}                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
parameters {                                                                                                                                                                                                      
    real<lower=0> colsizes[M];                                                                                                                                                                                    
    int<lower=0> noise[N,M];  # Noise                                                                                                                                                                             
    int<lower=0> counts[N,M];  # True counts                                                                                                                                                                      
    real<lower=0> countslambda[N];  # Rate for true counts                                                                                                                                                        
}                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
model {                                                                                                                                                                                                           
    countslambda ~ lognormal(2, 3);                                                                                                                                                                               
    for (n in 1:N) {                                                                                                                                                                                              
        for (m in 1:M) {                                                                                                                                                                                          
            noise[n,m] ~ poisson(colsizes[m]);                                                                                                                                                                    
            counts[n,m] ~ poisson(countslambda[n] * colsizes[m]);                                                                                                                                                 
        }                                                                                                                                                                                                         
    }                                                                                                                                                                                                             
    # obs <- noise + counts;                                                                                                                                                                                      
}                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
'                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
# Fit the model                                                                                                                                                                                                   
fit <- stan(model_code=stan.code)

messages.author: 3f22b207863d2049
messages.subject: Re: Noisy Poisson counts
parts:
Hi John,

Stan should be fine for modeling count data, but like you say, doesn't allow integer parameters (HMC requires some transformation of the parameters to be continuous over the entire real plane). If you really really need integer parameters, the only solution is to marginalize over all possible values of the integer parameters by defining a mixture model (see the chapter on mixture models in the Stan manual). In some cases, you can marginalize things analytically, which may the case in your model.

From your code it seems that you assume that the true counts and noise counts each follow independent Poisson distributions with rates counts.lambda[n] and noise.lambda, where the latter is hardcoded to 1. By definition, the sum of two independent Poisson variables X and Y again follows a Poisson distribution with rate (lambda_x + lambda_y), so in your case for each row n the rate is (counts.lambda[n] + noise.lambda). In other words, within each row, the sampling error in the data is still Poisson (i.e. variance equal to the mean), and you might just as well model the data as being Poisson-distributed with a parameter lambda[n] = counts.lambda[n] + noise.lambda, where the latter should also be defined as a continuous parameter.

In this particular example code, you assume to know the distribution of counts.lambda[n]. However, in your empirical dataset, this may not be true as you only observe the total counts (noise + true). If so, there is no way to identify what part is noise and what is true (lambda.noise could be anywhere between zero and the lowest overall rate in any of the n rows), and could just as well model the data as being Poisson-distributed with lambda[n] defined as a parameter, leaving counts.lambda[n] and noise.lambda unidentified.

Best,

Luc

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Noisy Poisson counts
parts:
Stan requires you to program the log probability function for
your model. It only supports continuous parameters. If you
have discrete parameters, they need to be marginalized out.

You're in luck with this model, because the Poisson is
well behaved:

if x1 ~ Poisson(lambda1) and x2 ~ Poisson(lambda2),
then x1 + x2 ~ Poisson(lambda1 + lambda2),

so you can replace this:

> noise[n,m] ~ poisson(colsizes[m]);
> counts[n,m] ~ poisson(countslambda[n] * colsizes[m]);
> # obs <- noise + counts;

with

obs ~ poisson(colsizes[m] + countslambda[n] * colsizes[m]);

and then you can get just eliminate the discrete
parameters noise[n,m] and counts[n,m]. I'd also be inclined
to rename the continuous parameters like countslambda and
colsizes with names that don't suggest their integer valued.
Though Andrew does like to name variables after their "standard"
name, so he might use lambda_counts for the mean parameter for
a discrete observed quantity counts.

I'm not sure exactly what you're trying to do, but given that
countslambda and colsizes are parameters constrained to be > 0,
you might consider dropping the constraint and instead exponentiating
the result --- that's the usual GLM form for Poisson regression.

- Bob

You can get a kind of soft identification with priors, hierarchical or
constant, but it's better to parameterize the model to get identification.

- Bob

messages.author: fb40a65bd21dcf6f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Noisy Poisson counts
parts:
Thanks for your answers. That all makes sense. I have to admit I was just using the Poisson as an example. I want to move to a negative binomial and perhaps test other distributions for the noise and the true counts. So the additivity property of Poissons isn't going to help in the long run. Also, I can see it is going to be inefficient to integrate out all the possible noise values. I think I might move to a mixture model. My counts appear to have a bimodal distribution with one mode close to 0.

Thanks for your help,
John.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Noisy Poisson counts
parts:
There's a description of how to do zero-inflated models and
hurdle models in the manual if you just literally need a 0-inflation
rather than a mixture of two Poissons or something.

The negative binomial is a gamma mixture of Poissons, and you
can often use the same trick to model the mean of a poisson as
a latent continuous parameter so you don't need to worry about
explicitly marginalizing out a discrete parameter.

- Bob

messages.author: 20758fda448fdbda
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Noisy Poisson counts
parts:
For what it is worth, if two negative binomials have the same variance-to-mean ratio (or beta in the r/beta parametrization) then their sum is negative binomial with the same V2M and r = sum(r_i). If the betas are not the same, all bets are off, of course.

Avi

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Noisy Poisson counts
parts:
You probably want to look at either hurdle or zero-inflated models,
both of which are ways of adding extra mass at 0 in a Poisson-based model.
Both are implemented as mixtures in Stan. I'm including them explicitly
in the next manual.

- Bob
